work.summary: Conducted research in the ARoS Lab under Prof. Edgar Lobaton. Designed a data collection protocol and built a dual-modal cough-speech dataset using both air and bone conduction microphones. Developed a dual-path contrastive learning architecture for robust cough-speech detection.

work.company: School of Engineering, Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
work.summary: Addressed long-context challenges in multitrack symbolic music modeling by developing a multitrack symbolic music tokenizer to design compact discrete representations for symbolic music understanding and generation. The work explored residual vector quantization, interleaved ABC notation, and multimodal alignment for controllable, musically coherent outputs.

highlights: Developed LyricMidi, a lyric-aware symbolic music foundation model with attribute-wise masked pretraining and hybrid music-language embeddings, improving vocal-centric understanding while maintaining strong performance on symbolic music classification benchmarks.
Developed symbolic accompaniment generation systems that transform lead sheets into full piano arrangements and guitar tablature.
Pretrained a unified symbolic music foundation model across performance / score MIDI and ABC notation to support cross-modal downstream tasks such as transcription, PM2S, and conditional generation.
Developed an end-to-end generative PM2S system for translating performance MIDI into sheet music.

publications.name: Investigating the Representation of Backchannels and Fillers in Fine-tuned Language Models
publications.summary: This work investigates how fine-tuning strategies enhance language models’ ability to represent and generate backchannels and fillers in dialogue. Empirical analyses demonstrate improved clustering quality and more human-like language generation, showcasing the potential for adapting general LMs into pragmatic-aware conversational models.

publications.name: LyricMidi: Joint Music–Language Pretraining for Symbolic Music Understanding
publications.summary: This paper proposes a unified music–language pretraining framework that jointly models symbolic music events and lyrics. The model achieves consistent improvements on vocal-centric symbolic music understanding tasks while preserving general music representation performance.
